Running a 40B-parameter AI model on a 12GB GPU at 64 tokens/sec?

RustingStrata is challenging conventional local inference engines with some impressive benchmark results.

In a recent comparison using Recursive Flint UD-Q5_K_XL on an RTX 3060 12GB with 30GB system RAM:

64.6 tokens/sec decode speed vs. 48.6 with llama.cpp.
33% faster warm decoding.
1.14–1.30K tokens/sec prompt processing.
No reported quality degradation.

How does it achieve this? Two key optimizations:

Adaptive expert placement based on the generated response rather than just prompt routing.
Smarter RAM page management to keep frequently needed expert weights accessible.

The interesting part is that the model is larger than available VRAM, yet careful CPU-GPU memory management makes surprisingly fast inference possible.

This shows how much performance can still be unlocked through inference-engine optimizations without changing model weights.
